Subject: Open-model readiness & compatibility — next steps

Alex / Taylor — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

TL;DR: Pinecrest is primarily looking to reduce inference spend and remove single-vendor operational risk while preserving output fidelity for clinical triage prompts and patient-facing summaries. You currently use OpenAI + Anthropic; you need a seamless compatibility path (function-calling + streaming) and HIPAA-friendly options (VPC/KMS).

What we heard (pain points):
- Cost: API spend with OpenAI has spiked; goal is ~35–50% lower Opex on generation/embedding use.
- Lock-in & auditability: dependency on proprietary APIs + limited audit logs for compliance reviews.
- Latency at scale: occasional 90th percentile spikes during batch processing windows.
- Compatibility: prompt/response drift risk when switching models; function calling behavior is critical for your orchestrations.
- Security: SOC2 evidence, KMS support, and network isolation are required for PHI workloads.

Current stack you described:
- Primary: OpenAI for chat and embeddings.
- Secondary: Anthropic for higher-assurance LLM tasks (safety-sensitive summarization).
- Orchestration: internal service bus, partial caching layer, and a small on-prem vectorstore for recent records.

Success criteria (what will make this a win for Pinecrest):
1) Equivalent or better clinical accuracy on our evaluation prompt set (we'll need a sample set).
2) 90th percentile token latency < 250ms on the main interactive path (goal: <200ms).
3) 35%+ cost reduction on generation/embedding unit economics at target volume.
4) Deployment options: hosted + VPC/private option with KMS and audit logs for PHI.
5) Function-calling parity and streaming support for incremental UX.

Initial model shortlist (compatibility-first):
- Llama-3 / 13B (quantized variants for cost)
- Mistral-7B / Instant family
- RedPajama / Eleutheria-compatible checkpoints (for deterministic behavior testing)

Recommended next steps from Redwood:
1) You share a 20–30 prompt sample set (redacted) we can use for side-by-side quality and latency testing.
2) Redwood will scope a 2-week POC using 1–2 candidate models (we propose Llama-3-13B int8 + Mistral-7B int8) and provide orthogonal tests for function-calling/streaming parity.
3) Redwood to provide an initial cost model and SLA options (see attached SLA draft).
4) Schedule a technical review with Taylor + our infra lead to confirm KMS/VPC requirements (proposed date below).

Proposed timeline:
- Tech review (architecture deep dive) — Tue, 24 Nov, 11am PT
- POC kickoff — Tue, 01 Dec
- POC report & decision review — by Fri, 15 Dec

Attachments: pinecrest-current-llm-inventory.csv (your inventory export you shared), redwood-offerings-overview.pdf, SLA draft.

Can you confirm: (a) sample prompt delivery timeline (by end of week?), (b) availability for the 24 Nov architecture call, and (c) whether SOC2 / KMS are blockers or just part of procurement?

Thanks — I'll loop Ben and Neha internally once you confirm so we can get pricing and POC resourcing locked.

Best,

Quick notes on function-calling parity and validation approach:
- We run deterministic signature tests: given the same prompt and a fixed stubbed tool, validate the structured output and parseability across models.
- For streaming parity: we compare incremental token emission patterns and average per-chunk latency; if a model buffers then we flag it.
- For prompt drift: we run a calibrated A/B across their prompt set and measure task-level metrics (extraction accuracy, summary ROUGE/ROUGE-L, and safety filter false positive rate).
